hints: A pipe (|) runs each side as a separate process. The right-hand side of cmd | while read …; done is a CHILD process (a subshell) — anything it assigns to a variable dies with that subshell.
while read …; done < <(cmd) redirects input from a process substitution instead of a pipe — the while loop itself stays in your CURRENT shell, so its variable assignments survive after the loop ends.

Write predictions.txt with pipe=0, procsub=3, and why=... naming the subshell (e.g. 'the pipe's right-hand side runs in a subshell, so count changes are lost when it exits'). Then run counter.sh and compare — read the honor line first: the check can't tell whether you predicted before running, you're only cheating your own reps.
